## Integration only — do not merge

This PR combines the seven component PRs below for end-to-end testing and benchmarks. Review and merge the component PRs individually; this integration remains a draft reference.

| Source component | Upstream PR |
| --- | --- |
| 1: [Perf] mamba: write the deduplicated conv verify window as one tile | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46184 |
| 2: [Feat] gdn: run DFLASH and DSPARK verify on the ReplaySSM spec ring | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46185 |
| 3: [Perf] spec: radix top-k for speculative verify target probabilities | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46186 |
| 4: [Feat] spec: online acceptance estimator for drafts without a confidence head | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46187 |
| 5: [Perf] gdn: fold ReplaySSM compact history in one product per head group | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46188 |
| 6: [Feat] gdn: run target verify on packed ragged tokens (ReplaySSM) | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46189 |
| 7: [Feat] spec: confidence-scheduled compact verify for DFLASH | https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46190 |

Dependencies: component 5 requires 2; component 6 requires 1 and 2; component 7 requires 4, plus 6 for compact GDN verification. All seven component branches passed their applicable pre-commit hooks. GPU CI on the updated upstream base still requires maintainer approval.

---

## Motivation

Enable adaptive verification for DFlash on GDN models, using the existing DSpark planner. An online acceptance estimator supplies confidence for DFlash drafts without a confidence head; compact verification reduces target work as serving load rises.

This upstreams the integration tested in https://github.com/jianc99/sglang/pull/8, including its seven component changes. The implementation and original measurements are by Jian Chen and Zihan Zhang (@SubSir). This submission was prepared with AI assistance.

## Modifications

- Add online acceptance estimation and connect DFlash to DSpark budget selection, ragged packing, compact graphs, and cutoff acceptance.
- Support packed GDN verification and compact ReplaySSM state commits for DFlash/DSpark.
- Optimize convolution window stores and target-probability top-k selection.
- Add regression coverage for estimator behavior, acceptance cutoffs, ragged verification, GDN commits, convolution updates, and positions.

Enable with `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`, `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, and `--speculative-dspark-sps-table-path <table>`. Use the existing offline `sglang.benchmark.dspark_sps_profiler` to produce the cost table. Full launch/profiling settings and per-component diffs are in the [source integration](https://github.com/jianc99/sglang/pull/8).

Related work: #38897 (ragged GDN/varlen convolution), #42688 (ReplaySSM masking), #41916 (target probabilities), #44866 (online estimator), #42711 and #42717 (planner fixes). This PR combines these areas into the DFlash compact-verification path; reviewers may prefer to land independent components first.

## Accuracy Tests

Previously reported on the source integration on GB300 (not rerun after updating to current upstream):

- 345 unit/kernel tests passed for DFlash, DSpark, speculative decoding, and the estimator; 455 passed for convolution, ReplaySSM, and Mamba. Two `test_gdn_replayssm_spec_fold` cases also fail on the source base.
- ReplaySSM circular/direct commit memcheck: 7 tests, 133 subtests, no device-side errors.
- Greedy output parity was checked against autoregressive decoding. Near-tie floating-point differences remain; outputs are not universally token-identical. Detailed parity results and limitations are in the source integration.

Current upstream integration: `git diff --check` and all applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the 38 changed files (including ruff, formatting, AST checks, and CI test registration). GPU runtime tests still need CI; this submission was prepared on a Mac without CUDA.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Existing source-integration measurements: Qwen3.8-27B, DFlash 2 block size 8, four GB300 GPUs (TP4), SPEED-Bench first turns, temperature 1. Decode throughput below is concurrency times per-request decode rate after the first token.

| Concurrency | Autoregressive tok/s | Adaptive DFlash tok/s | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 247 | 649 | 2.63x |
| 64 | 9,266 | 13,465 | 1.45x |
| 128 | 13,219 | 16,792 | 1.27x |
| 256 | 18,810 | 21,020 | 1.12x |
| 512 | 22,858 | 22,424 | 0.98x |

The high-concurrency rows use `--stream-interval 4`, a request cap of 528, and graphs/cost profiling through batch 512. Baseline/high-concurrency cells are single runs; this is not a guarantee of no regression. The source PR also separates gains from system optimizations versus adaptive verification alone.

Known limitation: compact graph selection can be slower than static full-block verification at lower concurrency. Full-block routing to batch-size-keyed graphs is left for follow-up. Benchmarks have not been rerun on this updated upstream base.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit and kernel tests.
- [ ] Update rendered documentation.
- [x] Provide prior accuracy and speed results, with their limitations above.
- [ ] Run GPU CI on the updated upstream integration.

+"""Row-wise top-k of a score matrix, resolved once per platform."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_flashinfer_available
+from sglang.utils import LazyImport
+
+if is_flashinfer_available():
+    # Resolved on first call, like the renorm kernels.
+    _flashinfer_top_k = LazyImport("flashinfer", "top_k")
+else:
+    _flashinfer_top_k = None
+
+
+def radix_topk(scores: torch.Tensor, k: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """The ``k`` largest values of each row of ``scores`` and their int64 ids,
+    sorted descending.
+
+    FlashInfer's radix select reads each row once and is several times faster
+    than ``torch.topk`` on a large vocabulary. It runs in deterministic mode:
+    when values tie at the k-th place, which of the tied ids are returned is
+    fixed for a given input, but it may differ from ``torch.topk``'s choice.
+    Without FlashInfer, or for a tensor that is not on the GPU, this is
+    ``torch.topk``.
+    """
+    if _flashinfer_top_k is not None and scores.is_cuda:
+        # FlashInfer only reads dense rows.
+        return _flashinfer_top_k(
+            scores.contiguous(), k, sorted=True, deterministic=True
+        )
+    return torch.topk(scores, k, dim=-1)
+
+
+__all__ = ["radix_topk"]

+"""Kernels for the online draft acceptance estimator.
+
+``max_log_odds`` turns draft scores into the estimator's feature, the log-odds
+of the most likely draft token, and optionally the logistic prediction from it.
+``observe_acceptance`` folds verified drafts into the per-round Newton (IRLS)
+statistics and, every ``refit_interval`` calls, refits the logistic
+coefficients in place. Both read their state from device tensors only, so they
+never synchronize with the host and can be captured in a CUDA graph.
+"""
+
+from typing import Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+# Columns of the per-position statistics: the X^T W X arrowhead entries a, b, c,
+# the X^T r entries g0, g1, and the observation count n.
+NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS = 6
+# A refit halves a slope step that would make the slope non-positive at most
+# this many times before dropping it.
+_MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS = 8
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _max_log_odds_kernel(
+    scores_ptr,
+    stride_req,
+    stride_pos,
+    stride_cand,
+    temperatures_ptr,
+    temperatures_stride,
+    slope_ptr,
+    intercepts_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    probs_ptr,
+    num_positions,
+    num_candidates,
+    MAX_LOG_ODDS: tl.constexpr,
+    WITH_PROBS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    req = row // num_positions
+    pos = row % num_positions
+
+    # Rows with a non-positive temperature are greedy; score them at T = 1.
+    temperature = tl.load(temperatures_ptr + req * temperatures_stride).to(tl.float32)
+    temperature = tl.where(temperature > 0.0, temperature, 1.0)
+
+    row_ptr = scores_ptr + req.to(tl.int64) * stride_req + pos.to(tl.int64) * stride_pos
+
+    # logit(q_max) = log(q_max / (1 - q_max)) = -log(sum_{z != argmax} e^(z - m)),
+    # with m the max score. Track the running max and the sum over every other
+    # candidate directly, so confident rows keep their precision instead of
+    # cancelling in (sum_z e^(z - m)) - 1.
+    run_max = float("-inf")
+    run_rest = 0.0
+    for start in range(0, num_candidates, BLOCK_N):
+        offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+        mask = offs < num_candidates
+        s = tl.load(row_ptr + offs * stride_cand, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(
+            tl.float32
+        )
+        s = s / temperature
+        blk_max = tl.max(s, axis=0)
+        # Exclude exactly one instance of the block max; ties stay in the rest.
+        blk_arg = tl.min(tl.where(s == blk_max, offs, num_candidates), axis=0)
+        e = tl.where((s > float("-inf")) & (offs != blk_arg), tl.exp(s - blk_max), 0.0)
+        blk_rest = tl.sum(e, axis=0)
+        # Merge the block into the running pair; the smaller max joins the rest.
+        rest_new_max = blk_rest + (run_rest + 1.0) * tl.exp(run_max - blk_max)
+        rest_old_max = run_rest + tl.where(
+            blk_max > float("-inf"), (blk_rest + 1.0) * tl.exp(blk_max - run_max), 0.0
+        )
+        run_rest = tl.where(blk_max > run_max, rest_new_max, rest_old_max)
+        run_max = tl.maximum(run_max, blk_max)
+
+    feature = tl.where(run_rest > 0.0, -tl.log(run_rest), MAX_LOG_ODDS)
+    feature = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(feature, -MAX_LOG_ODDS), MAX_LOG_ODDS)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + row, feature)
+    if WITH_PROBS:
+        bias = tl.load(intercepts_ptr + pos)
+        tl.store(probs_ptr + row, tl.sigmoid(tl.load(slope_ptr) * feature + bias))
+
+
+def max_log_odds(
+    scores: torch.Tensor,
+    temperatures: torch.Tensor,
+    clamp: float,
+    slope: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    intercepts: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Log-odds of the most likely candidate of each temperature-scaled row.
+
+    scores: [bs, num_positions, num_candidates] logits; temperatures: one per
+    request (any shape with bs elements). Returns the float32 log-odds
+    [bs, num_positions], clamped to +-clamp, and, when the float32 logistic
+    coefficients slope [1] and intercepts [num_positions] are given, the
+    probabilities sigmoid(slope * x + intercepts[k]) from the same launch
+    (otherwise None).
+
+    One program handles one row and walks its candidates in blocks, so the
+    kernel is sized for candidate lists; a full-vocabulary row runs serially.
+    """
+    bs, num_positions, num_candidates = scores.shape
+    temperatures = temperatures.reshape(-1)
+    assert temperatures.numel() == bs, (temperatures.shape, scores.shape)
+    with_probs = slope is not None
+    assert with_probs == (intercepts is not None)
+    if with_probs:
+        assert slope.numel() == 1 and intercepts.shape == (num_positions,)

+"""Online per-position acceptance estimator for drafts without a confidence head.
+
+Confidence-scheduled verification needs the probability that each draft token
+is accepted given that every earlier one was. A draft model without a trained
+confidence head gets it from a logistic model calibrated while serving:
+
+    p_k = sigmoid(slope * x_k + bias_k)
+
+where x_k = logit(q_max) is the log-odds of the most likely token of the draft
+distribution at position k, slope is shared by all positions and bias_k is
+per position. The feature scores the draft distribution, not the sampled
+token, so trimming drafts by it never conditions on the trimmed token and
+rejection sampling stays lossless.
+
+The coefficients are refit by one damped Newton (IRLS) step every
+``refit_interval`` observations. Everything stays on the device and no call
+synchronizes with the host, so the estimator runs under overlap scheduling and
+inside CUDA graphs. All state updates are deterministic, so ranks that observe
+identical inputs keep identical coefficients.
+"""
+
+from typing import Tuple
+
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.acceptance_estimator import (
+    NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS,
+    max_log_odds,
+    observe_acceptance,
+)
+
+# The feature log(q / (1 - q)) is infinite for a row with all of its mass on one
+# token; clamp it symmetrically.
+_MAX_LOG_ODDS = 40.0
+# Cold-start coefficients. Log-loss is flat near the optimum, so one starting
+# point serves typical draft models and the first refits replace it.
+_INIT_SLOPE = 0.5
+_INIT_BIAS = -0.2
+# Newton steps are damped by n / (n + _DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS): a round with this
+# many observations moves a coefficient half of a full step, so data-poor
+# positions keep learning, only slowly.
+_DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS = 50.0
+# Ridge on the Newton solve.
+_L2 = 1e-3
+# Rows of requests the observe kernel processes per iteration.
+_MAX_BLOCK_REQS = 256
+
+
+class OnlineAcceptanceEstimator:
+    """Per-position conditional acceptance probabilities from draft confidence.
+
+    Per verify step the caller:
+    1. ``feature_from_scores`` on the draft scores of each position,
+    2. ``predict`` to get the conditional acceptance probabilities,
+    3. after verification, ``observe`` with the same features and the verify
+       outcome.
+    ``feature_and_predict`` does steps 1 and 2 in one kernel launch.
+    ``observe`` evaluates the Newton weights at the current coefficients, so it
+    may run before or after the next step's ``predict``.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_positions: int,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        refit_interval: int = 100,
+    ) -> None:
+        assert num_positions > 0 and max_num_reqs > 0 and refit_interval > 0
+        self.num_positions = num_positions
+        self.refit_interval = refit_interval
+        self._block_reqs = min(triton.next_power_of_2(max_num_reqs), _MAX_BLOCK_REQS)
+        # Coefficients are updated in place, so CUDA graphs that read them stay
+        # valid across refits.
+        self.slope = torch.full((1,), _INIT_SLOPE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        self.intercepts = torch.full(
+            (num_positions,), _INIT_BIAS, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+        )
+        # Per-round Newton statistics per position, cleared at every refit.
+        self._stats = torch.zeros(
+            (num_positions, NUM_ACCEPTANCE_STATS), dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+        )
+        # observe() calls since the last refit.
+        self._num_calls = torch.zeros((1,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    def feature_from_scores(
+        self, scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """scores [bs, num_positions, num_candidates]: the draft logits each
+        position sampled from; temperatures: per request, greedy rows <= 0.
+        Returns logit(q_max) of the temperature-scaled rows, float32
+        [bs, num_positions]."""
+        assert scores.dim() == 3 and scores.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return max_log_odds(scores, temperatures, _MAX_LOG_ODDS)[0]
+
+    def feature_and_predict(
+        self, scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """``feature_from_scores`` and ``predict`` fused into one kernel launch.
+        Returns the features and the conditional acceptance probabilities, both
+        float32 [bs, num_positions]. Does not change any state."""
+        assert scores.dim() == 3 and scores.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return max_log_odds(
+            scores, temperatures, _MAX_LOG_ODDS, self.slope, self.intercepts
+        )
+
+    def predict(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Conditional acceptance probability of each draft position, float32
+        [bs, num_positions]. Does not change any state."""
+        assert x.dim() == 2 and x.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        return torch.sigmoid(torch.addcmul(self.intercepts, x.float(), self.slope))
+
+    def observe(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        num_verified: torch.Tensor,
+        num_accepted: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Learn from one verify step.
+
+        x: the features the verified drafts were predicted with, [bs,
+        num_positions]; num_verified: draft tokens the target verified per
+        request, the anchor excluded; num_accepted: how many of them it
+        accepted, the bonus token excluded. Positions up to and including the
+        first rejection are observed, labelled by whether they were accepted.
+        Rows with num_verified = 0 contribute nothing and their features are
+        not read, so padding rows must pass 0. Every ``refit_interval``-th
+        call refits the coefficients and starts a new round.
+
+        This updates the estimator, so run it (or replay a graph that captured
+        it) exactly once per real verify step, never in warmup or dummy
+        forwards.
+        """
+        assert x.dim() == 2 and x.shape[1] == self.num_positions
+        assert num_verified.numel() == num_accepted.numel() == x.shape[0]
+        observe_acceptance(
+            x,
+            num_verified.reshape(-1).contiguous(),
+            num_accepted.reshape(-1).contiguous(),
+            self.slope,
+            self.intercepts,
+            self._stats,
+            self._num_calls,
+            refit_interval=self.refit_interval,
+            l2=_L2,
+            damping=_DAMPING_OBSERVATIONS,
+            block_reqs=self._block_reqs,
+        )

+"""GDN ReplaySSM circular commit: fold and track the compact history.
+
+The folded and tracked checkpoints must match a float64 reference of the same
+closed form for several value/key head ratios, both checkpoint dtypes, a
+partial V tile, slot-strided and layer-inner state pools, null rows, rings of
+16 to 128 steps (histories longer than one fold chunk), with and without track
+rows, and with bf16 rings plus residuals or fp32 rings without them. Ring
+entries past the committed history are NaN and must not be read, and every
+slot the commit does not own stays bit-identical. Every case runs through both

+appends the draft window to the compact request ring; the commit folds the

+    g = -torch.exp(layer.A_log.double()) * F.softplus(
+        a.double() + layer.dt_bias.double()
+    )
+    beta = torch.sigmoid(b.double())
+    state = ssm_state.double()
+    outputs, states = [], []
+    for t in range(steps):
+        state = state * torch.exp(g[t])[:, None, None]
+        delta = beta[t][:, None] * (v[t] - torch.einsum("hvk,hk->hv", state, k[t]))
+        state = state + delta[:, :, None] * k[t][:, None, :]
+        outputs.append(torch.einsum("hvk,hk->hv", state, q[t]))
+        states.append(state)
+    windows = [x[:, t + 1 : t + CONV_WIDTH] for t in range(steps)]
+    return torch.stack(outputs), states, windows
+
+
+def _relative_error(actual, expected):
+    expected = expected.double()
+    error = (actual.double() - expected).abs().max()
+    return (error / expected.abs().max().clamp(min=1e-30)).item()

+    def test_chain_matches_reference(self):

+        snapshot path, without error growth, and touch nothing outside the

+    def test_lazy_fold_chain_replays_history(self):

+        window would not fit the ring, so verifies replay committed history;
+        the outputs stay as close to the reference as the snapshot path's."""

+    def _check_chain(self, ssm_dtype, num_steps, lazy=False):
+        torch.manual_seed(7)
+        layers = _make_layers()
+        template = _template(ssm_dtype)
+        req_rows, cache_indices = _rows_and_slots()
+        real_rows, real_slots = req_rows[:NUM_REAL], cache_indices[:NUM_REAL].long()
+        qsl = torch.arange(
+            0, NUM_SLOTS * WIDTH + 1, WIDTH, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        arms = {
+            "replayssm": _Arm(
+                template,
+                replayssm=True,
+                dispatcher=self.dispatcher,
+                ring_len=4 * WIDTH if lazy else RING,
+                lazy=lazy,
+            ),
+            # The Triton recurrent verify writes a snapshot per draft on every
+            # GPU.
+            "snapshot": _Arm(template, replayssm=False, dispatcher=self.dispatcher),
+        }
+        backends = {name: arm.backend(qsl, cache_indices) for name, arm in arms.items()}
+        replayssm = arms["replayssm"]
+        untouched_rows = [
+            r for r in range(NUM_ROWS) if r not in set(real_rows.tolist())
+        ]
+        untouched_slots = [
+            s for s in range(NUM_POOL_SLOTS) if s not in set(real_slots.tolist())
+        ]
+        ring_before = replayssm.state.replayssm_d[:, untouched_rows].clone()
+        reference = {
+            "temporal": template["temporal"].double(),
+            "conv": template["conv"].double(),
+        }
+        # Under the lazy fold the checkpoint lags the committed state by the
+        # history kept in the ring, so only the outputs are compared; they
+        # depend on the checkpoint and the replayed history together.
+        keys = ("out",) if lazy else ("out", "state")
+        errors = {name: {key: [] for key in keys} for name in arms}
+        batch = _batch(NUM_SLOTS * WIDTH, req_rows)
+        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(11)
+        expected_base = torch.zeros(NUM_REAL, dtype=torch.int64)
+        max_history = 0
+        for _ in range(num_steps):
+            inputs = _dense_inputs()
+            accept = torch.randint(1, WIDTH + 1, (NUM_REAL,), generator=generator)
+            outputs = {
+                name: _verify(backends[name], layers, batch, inputs) for name in arms
+            }
+            ref_out = []
+            for layer, (mixed_qkv, a, b) in zip(layers, inputs):
+                layer_out = []
+                for i in range(NUM_REAL):
+                    slot, n = int(real_slots[i]), int(accept[i])
+                    rows = slice(i * WIDTH, (i + 1) * WIDTH)
+                    out, states, windows = _gdn_reference(
+                        layer,
+                        reference["conv"][layer.layer_id, slot],
+                        reference["temporal"][layer.layer_id, slot],
+                        mixed_qkv[rows],
+                        a[rows],
+                        b[rows],
+                    )
+                    layer_out.append(out)
+                    reference["temporal"][layer.layer_id, slot] = states[n - 1]
+                    reference["conv"][layer.layer_id, slot] = windows[n - 1]
+                ref_out.append(torch.cat(layer_out))
+            for name, arm in arms.items():
+                arm.commit((accept - 1).cuda(), req_rows[:NUM_REAL])
+                out = torch.stack(
+                    [
+                        o.reshape(-1, V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM)[: NUM_REAL * WIDTH]
+                        for o in outputs[name]
+                    ]
+                )
+                errors[name]["out"].append(_relative_error(out, torch.stack(ref_out)))
+                if not lazy:
+                    errors[name]["state"].append(
+                        _relative_error(
+                            arm.state.temporal[:, real_slots],
+                            reference["temporal"][:, real_slots],
+                        )
+                    )
+                # Conv rollback is an exact copy of the accepted inputs.
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(
+                        arm.state.conv[0][:, real_slots].double(),
+                        reference["conv"][:, real_slots],
+                    ),
+                    name,
+                )
+            # The graph-padding slot (state -1) outputs zeros.
+            for out in outputs["replayssm"]:
+                padding = out.reshape(-1, V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM)[NUM_REAL * WIDTH :]
+                self.assertEqual(padding.abs().max().item(), 0.0)
+            pool = replayssm.pool
+            if lazy:
+                history = pool.replayssm_spec_write_pos[real_rows]
+                max_history = max(max_history, int(history.max()))
+                continue
+            # Cursors: folded and reset every commit, ring origin advanced.
+            expected_base = (expected_base + accept) % RING
+            self.assertEqual(
+                pool.replayssm_spec_write_pos[real_rows].abs().sum().item(), 0
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(pool.replayssm_is_flush[real_rows].abs().sum().item(), 0)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                pool.replayssm_cache_base[real_rows].cpu().tolist(),
+                expected_base.tolist(),
+            )
+
+        if lazy:
+            # Later verifies saw committed history.
+            self.assertGreater(max_history, WIDTH)
+        pool = replayssm.pool
+        for cursor in (
+            pool.replayssm_spec_write_pos,
+            pool.replayssm_cache_base,
+            pool.replayssm_is_flush,
+        ):
+            self.assertEqual(cursor[untouched_rows].abs().sum().item(), 0)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(replayssm.state.replayssm_d[:, untouched_rows], ring_before)
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                replayssm.state.temporal[:, untouched_slots],
+                template["temporal"][:, untouched_slots],
+            )
+        )
+
+        # Relative errors: mean over the chain, early window (after a burn-in
+        # that lets the state reach its working magnitude) and late window.
+        def mean(values):
+            return sum(values) / len(values)
+
+        summary = {
+            name: {
+                key: (mean(values), mean(values[32:96]), mean(values[-64:]))
+                for key, values in errs.items()
+            }
+            for name, errs in errors.items()
+        }
+        print(f"\n{ssm_dtype} relative error (mean, early, late): {summary}")
+        for key in keys:
+            values = errors["replayssm"][key]
+            chain_mean, early, late = summary["replayssm"][key]
+            self.assertTrue(all(map(math.isfinite, values)), key)
+            # No error growth over the chain.
+            self.assertLessEqual(late, 2 * early + 1e-6, f"{ssm_dtype} {key}")
+            # Within rounding of the snapshot path on the same inputs: the
+            # verify dots round their operands to bf16 (bf16 state) or TF32
+            # (fp32 state), as the snapshot kernels do.
+            baseline = summary["snapshot"][key][0]
+            self.assertLessEqual(chain_mean, 1.25 * baseline, f"{ssm_dtype} {key}")

+    def test_track_slot_holds_tracked_step(self):
+        """A track slot receives the state and conv window of its tracked step
+        and leaves the active commit unchanged; step -1 tracks nothing."""
+        for ssm_dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
+            with self.subTest(ssm_dtype=ssm_dtype):
+                self._check_track(ssm_dtype)

+    def _check_track(self, ssm_dtype):
+        torch.manual_seed(99)
+        layers = _make_layers()
+        template = _template(ssm_dtype)
+        req_rows, cache_indices = _rows_and_slots()
+        real_rows = req_rows[:NUM_REAL]
+        active = cache_indices[:NUM_REAL].long()
+        unused = [s for s in range(NUM_POOL_SLOTS) if s not in set(active.tolist())]
+        track_slots = torch.tensor(unused[:NUM_REAL], device="cuda")
+        accept = torch.tensor([8, 5, 3, 1, 6, 8], device="cuda")
+        track_steps = torch.tensor([7, 2, -1, 0, 5, 3], device="cuda")
+        qsl = torch.arange(
+            0, NUM_SLOTS * WIDTH + 1, WIDTH, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        batch = _batch(NUM_SLOTS * WIDTH, req_rows)
+        tracked, plain, at_step = (self._replayssm(template) for _ in range(3))
+        backends = [
+            arm.backend(qsl, cache_indices) for arm in (tracked, plain, at_step)
+        ]
+
+        # Warm-up steps move the ring origin off zero.
+        for _ in range(3):
+            inputs = _dense_inputs()
+            warm_accept = torch.randint(1, WIDTH + 1, (NUM_REAL,), device="cuda")
+            for arm, backend in zip((tracked, plain, at_step), backends):
+                _verify(backend, layers, batch, inputs)
+                arm.commit(warm_accept - 1, real_rows)
+        before = tracked.state.temporal.clone()
+
+        inputs = _dense_inputs()
+        for backend in backends:
+            _verify(backend, layers, batch, inputs)
+        tracked.commit(accept - 1, real_rows, track_slots, track_steps)
+        plain.commit(accept - 1, real_rows)
+        at_step.commit(
+            torch.where(track_steps >= 0, track_steps, accept - 1), real_rows
+        )
+
+        # The active commit does not see the track slots. Compiling the track
+        # path in may change the rounding of the active fold by one ulp.
+        eps = torch.finfo(ssm_dtype).eps
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            tracked.state.temporal[:, active].float(),
+            plain.state.temporal[:, active].float(),
+            rtol=eps,
+            atol=1e-6,
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                tracked.state.conv[0][:, active], plain.state.conv[0][:, active]
+            )
+        )
+        for i, step in enumerate(track_steps.tolist()):
+            track = int(track_slots[i])
+            if step < 0:
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(tracked.state.temporal[:, track], before[:, track])
+                )
+                continue
+            # The tracked state is the active state of a commit that accepted
+            # exactly the tracked step (same fold, one rounding).
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                tracked.state.temporal[:, track].float(),
+                at_step.state.temporal[:, int(active[i])].float(),
+                rtol=eps,
+                atol=1e-6,
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(
+                    tracked.state.conv[0][:, track],
+                    at_step.state.conv[0][:, int(active[i])],
+                )
+            )

+    def _check_ragged(self, ssm_dtype, real_lens, num_slots, num_tokens):

+        # The dense arm holds the same real tokens and random padding steps.
+        packed_inputs, dense_inputs = [], _dense_inputs(num_slots)
+        for dense in dense_inputs:
+            packed = tuple(_randn(num_tokens, x.shape[1]) for x in dense)

+"""Speculative verify target probabilities: selecting the top-k on the raw logits
+and dividing only the selected values by the temperature must give the same
+distribution as dividing the whole vocabulary first and running ``torch.topk``.
+
+When several logits tie at a row's top-k boundary, which of them keep the mass
+is chosen deterministically but may differ from ``torch.topk``; the kept count
+and the probability values are the same."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+import sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.topk as topk_ops
+from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.topk import radix_topk
+from sglang.srt.speculative.dflash_utils import (
+    _dflash_top_p_renorm_prob,
+    build_speculative_verify_target_probs,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+_DEVICES = ["cpu"] + (["cuda"] if torch.cuda.is_available() else [])
+_DRAFT_TOKEN_NUM = 8
+
+
+def _skip_unsupported_top_p(device, need_top_p):
+    # The top-p renormalization kernel is resolved for the accelerator only.
+    if need_top_p and device == "cpu":
+        pytest.skip("top-p renormalization needs the accelerator kernel")
+
+
+def _case(device, logits, top_ks, *, need_top_p, seed, temperature=None):
+    """Sampling params for ``len(top_ks)`` requests and the call kwargs."""
+    bs = len(top_ks)
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+    if temperature is None:
+        temperatures = 0.2 + 1.6 * torch.rand((bs,), generator=g, device=device)
+    else:
+        temperatures = torch.full((bs,), temperature, device=device)
+    info = SimpleNamespace(
+        temperatures=temperatures.view(-1, 1),
+        top_ks=torch.tensor(top_ks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        top_ps=0.5 + 0.5 * torch.rand((bs,), generator=g, device=device),
+        need_top_k_sampling=True,
+        need_top_p_sampling=need_top_p,
+    )
+    uniform = top_ks[0] if len(set(top_ks)) == 1 else None
+    return dict(
+        next_token_logits=logits,
+        sampling_info=info,
+        draft_token_num=logits.shape[0] // bs,
+        bs=bs,
+        max_top_k=max(top_ks),
+        uniform_top_k_value=uniform,
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(next_token_logits, sampling_info, draft_token_num, bs, max_top_k, **_):
+    """The previous implementation: scale the whole vocabulary, then top-k."""
+    info = sampling_info
+    temperature = torch.repeat_interleave(info.temperatures, draft_token_num, dim=0)
+    scaled = next_token_logits / temperature
+    top_ks = torch.repeat_interleave(info.top_ks, draft_token_num, dim=0).long()
+    top_vals, top_ids = torch.topk(scaled, k=max_top_k, dim=-1)
+    ranks = torch.arange(max_top_k, device=scaled.device)[None, :]
+    top_vals = top_vals.masked_fill(ranks >= top_ks[:, None], float("-inf"))
+    top_probs = F.softmax(top_vals, dim=-1)
+    if info.need_top_p_sampling:
+        top_probs = _dflash_top_p_renorm_prob(
+            top_probs, torch.repeat_interleave(info.top_ps, draft_token_num, dim=0)
+        )
+    probs = torch.zeros_like(scaled).scatter_(1, top_ids, top_probs)
+    return probs.view(bs, draft_token_num, -1)
+
+
+def _random_logits(device, rows, vocab, seed):
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
+    return 4.0 * torch.randn((rows, vocab), generator=g, device=device)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("need_top_p", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "vocab,top_ks",
+    [
+        (1000, [20, 20, 20, 20]),  # uniform top-k, no per-row mask
+        (1000, [1, 20, 7, 64]),  # mixed, including a greedy row
+        (151936, [1, 20, 7, 64]),
+        (151936, [2048] * 4),
+        (151936, [2049] * 4),
+        (151936, [4096] * 4),
+        (151936, [1, 4096, 2049, 20]),
+    ],
+)
+def test_matches_full_vocab_temperature(device, need_top_p, vocab, top_ks):
+    _skip_unsupported_top_p(device, need_top_p)
+    rows = len(top_ks) * _DRAFT_TOKEN_NUM
+    logits = _random_logits(device, rows, vocab, seed=vocab + max(top_ks))
+    kwargs = _case(device, logits, top_ks, need_top_p=need_top_p, seed=max(top_ks))
+    got = build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**kwargs)
+    want = _reference(**kwargs)
+    # Continuous random logits have no ties, so the selected sets agree and the
+    # probabilities are computed from identical values.
+    assert got.shape == want.shape and got.dtype == want.dtype
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, want, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    for i in (i for i, k in enumerate(top_ks) if k == 1):
+        assert torch.equal(
+            got[i].argmax(-1), logits.view(len(top_ks), -1, vocab)[i].argmax(-1)
+        )
+        assert torch.all(got[i].max(-1).values == 1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("need_top_p", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_ks", [[20] * 4, [1, 20, 2049, 5]])
+def test_vocab_masked_rows(device, need_top_p, top_ks):
+    """Grammar masks leave rows with fewer finite logits than k."""
+    _skip_unsupported_top_p(device, need_top_p)
+    rows, vocab = len(top_ks) * _DRAFT_TOKEN_NUM, 32000
+    logits = _random_logits(device, rows, vocab, seed=3)
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(4)
+    keep = torch.rand((rows, vocab), generator=g, device=device).argsort(-1)
+    finite = torch.zeros_like(logits, dtype=torch.bool)
+    for r in range(rows):
+        finite[r, keep[r, : r % 15 + 1]] = True
+    logits = logits.masked_fill(~finite, float("-inf"))
+    kwargs = _case(device, logits, top_ks, need_top_p=need_top_p, seed=5)
+    got = build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**kwargs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, _reference(**kwargs), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert torch.all(got.view(rows, vocab)[~finite] == 0)
+
+
+def _check_tied(got, want, logits, top_ks):
+    """``got`` is an exact top-k distribution: the right count of kept ids per
+    row, none of them below a dropped logit, and the reference probabilities."""
+    rows, vocab = logits.shape
+    got, want = got.view(rows, vocab), want.view(rows, vocab)
+    row_k = torch.tensor(top_ks, device=logits.device).repeat_interleave(
+        rows // len(top_ks)
+    )
+    kept = got > 0
+    assert torch.equal(kept.sum(-1), row_k)
+    min_kept = logits.masked_fill(~kept, float("inf")).min(-1).values
+    max_dropped = logits.masked_fill(kept, float("-inf")).max(-1).values
+    assert torch.all(min_kept >= max_dropped)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        got.sort(-1, descending=True).values,
+        want.sort(-1, descending=True).values,
+        rtol=0,
+        atol=0,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_ks", [[20, 20], [3, 20], [1, 4096]])
+def test_ties_at_the_k_boundary(device, top_ks):
+    """Integer logits tie at every row's own boundary, also in a mixed batch
+    where a row's k is below the selected max_top_k."""
+    rows, vocab = len(top_ks) * _DRAFT_TOKEN_NUM, 50000
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(6)
+    logits = torch.randint(0, 6, (rows, vocab), generator=g, device=device).float()
+    kwargs = _case(device, logits, top_ks, need_top_p=False, seed=7)
+    got = build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**kwargs)
+    assert torch.equal(got, build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**kwargs))
+    _check_tied(got, _reference(**kwargs), logits, top_ks)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+def test_ties_created_by_the_temperature(device):
+    """Two logits one ulp apart can round to one value after the division.
+    Selecting on the raw logits keeps the larger one, a valid top-k of the
+    scaled logits, with the reference probabilities."""
+    vocab, k, temperature = 4096, 8, 3.7
+    # A tensor, not a Python scalar: CUDA multiplies by the reciprocal of a
+    # scalar divisor, which rounds differently from the verify path.
+    t = torch.full((1,), temperature, device=device)
+    x = torch.tensor(1.9999, device=device)
+    for _ in range(4096):
+        y = torch.nextafter(x, x + 1)
+        if x / t == y / t:
+            break
+        x = y
+    assert x / t == y / t
+    logits = _random_logits(device, 2, vocab, seed=8).clamp(max=1.0)
+    logits[:, : k - 1] = torch.arange(10.0, 10.0 + k - 1, device=device)
+    logits[:, 100], logits[:, 101] = y, x  # compete for the k-th place
+    kwargs = _case(
+        device, logits, [k], need_top_p=False, seed=9, temperature=temperature
+    )
+    got = build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**kwargs)
+    want = _reference(**kwargs)
+    _check_tied(got, want, logits / t, [k])
+    assert torch.all((got.view(2, vocab)[:, 100:102] > 0).sum(-1) == 1)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+def test_torch_fallback(device, monkeypatch):

+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("k", [1, 20, 2048, 2049, 4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("strided", [False, True])
+def test_radix_topk_matches_torch(device, dtype, k, strided):
+    g = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(k)
+    scores = torch.randn((37, 2 * 151936), generator=g, device=device).to(dtype)
+    # A column slice is not contiguous; the op must still read it correctly.
+    scores = scores[:, ::2] if strided else scores[:, :151936].contiguous()
+    values, ids = radix_topk(scores, k)

+    torch.testing.assert_close(scores.gather(-1, ids), ref_values, rtol=0, atol=0)

+def _ref_feature(scores: torch.Tensor, temperatures: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """logit(q_max) of the temperature-scaled rows, in float64."""
+    temps = temperatures.reshape(-1).double()
+    temps = torch.where(temps > 0, temps, torch.ones_like(temps))
+    s = scores.double() / temps[:, None, None]
+    top, arg = s.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    rest = torch.exp(s - top).scatter(-1, arg, 0.0).sum(dim=-1)
+    return (-torch.log(rest)).clamp(-_MAX_LOG_ODDS, _MAX_LOG_ODDS)

+class _RefEstimator:
+    """Float64 reference of the estimator round: observation rule, IRLS
+    statistics, damped Newton refit and the reset after every refit."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_positions: int,
+        refit_interval: int,
+        init_slope: float = _INIT_SLOPE,
+        max_slope_halvings: int = _MAX_SLOPE_HALVINGS,
+    ):
+        self.k = num_positions
+        self.refit_interval = refit_interval
+        self.max_slope_halvings = max_slope_halvings
+        self.slope = torch.tensor(init_slope, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.bias = torch.full((num_positions,), _INIT_BIAS, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.stats = torch.zeros(num_positions, 6, dtype=torch.float64)
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def predict(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.sigmoid(self.slope * x.double() + self.bias)
+
+    def observe(self, x, num_verified, num_accepted):
+        x = x.double().cpu()
+        verified = num_verified.cpu().long()[:, None]
+        accepted = num_accepted.cpu().long()[:, None]
+        pos = torch.arange(self.k)[None, :]
+        observed = (pos <= accepted) & (pos < verified)
+        label = (pos < accepted).double()
+        p = self.predict(x)
+        w = torch.where(observed, p * (1 - p), 0.0)
+        r = torch.where(observed, label - p, 0.0)
+        x = torch.where(observed, x, 0.0)
+        self.stats += torch.stack(
+            [
+                (w * x * x).sum(0),
+                (w * x).sum(0),
+                w.sum(0),
+                (r * x).sum(0),
+                r.sum(0),
+                observed.double().sum(0),
+            ],
+            dim=1,
+        )
+        self.calls += 1
+        if self.calls >= self.refit_interval:
+            self._refit()
+
+    def _refit(self):
+        a, b, c, g0, g1, n = self.stats.unbind(1)
+        # Dense solve of (X^T W X + L2 I) d = X^T r for the slope step.
+        hess = torch.zeros(self.k + 1, self.k + 1, dtype=torch.float64)
+        hess[0, 0] = a.sum()
+        hess[0, 1:] = b
+        hess[1:, 0] = b
+        hess[1:, 1:] = torch.diag(c)
+        hess += _L2 * torch.eye(self.k + 1, dtype=torch.float64)
+        grad = torch.cat([g0.sum()[None], g1])
+        step_slope = torch.linalg.solve(hess, grad)[0]
+        step_slope = step_slope * n.sum() / (n.sum() + _DAMPING)
+        # Backtrack until the slope stays positive, else drop the step.
+        for _ in range(self.max_slope_halvings):
+            if self.slope + step_slope > 0:
+                break
+            step_slope = step_slope / 2
+        if not torch.isfinite(step_slope) or self.slope + step_slope <= 0:
+            step_slope = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.float64)
+        # Intercepts: exact Newton step given the (damped) slope step, damped.
+        step_bias = (g1 - b * step_slope) / (c + _L2) * n / (n + _DAMPING)
+        step_bias = torch.where(torch.isfinite(step_bias), step_bias, 0.0)
+        self.slope = self.slope + step_slope
+        self.bias = self.bias + step_bias
+        self.stats.zero_()
+        self.calls = 0
+
+
+def _random_step(gen, bs, k, true_slope, true_bias, device):
+    """One verify step of synthetic drafts: features, then a verify outcome
+    drawn from the true logistic model, with some requests verifying fewer than
+    k drafts."""
+    x = (torch.randn(bs, k, generator=gen) * 3.0 + 2.0).clamp(
+        -_MAX_LOG_ODDS, _MAX_LOG_ODDS
+    )
+    p = torch.sigmoid(true_slope * x + true_bias)
+    hits = (torch.rand(bs, k, generator=gen) < p).int()
+    leading = torch.cumprod(hits, dim=1).sum(dim=1)
+    verified = torch.randint(0, k + 1, (bs,), generator=gen)
+    verified = torch.where(torch.rand(bs, generator=gen) < 0.7, k, verified)
+    accepted = torch.minimum(leading, verified)
+    return (
+        x.to(device),
+        verified.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        accepted.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+    )

+    weight = torch.randn(dim, width, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    bias = torch.randn(dim, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    num_accept_tokens = None
+    state_len = width - 1
+    if case == "accept_offset":
+        num_accept_tokens = torch.randint(
+            1, seqlen + 1, (batch,), device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        state_len += seqlen - 1
+    conv_state = torch.randn(num_slots, dim, state_len, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    slots = torch.randperm(num_slots, device=device)[: 2 * batch].to(torch.int32)
+    conv_state_indices, window_indices = slots[:batch].clone(), slots[batch:]
+    if with_padding:
+        conv_state_indices[0] = conv_state_indices[-1] = PAD_SLOT_ID
+    real = conv_state_indices != PAD_SLOT_ID
+
+    # MambaPool._allocate_deduplicated_conv_window: one row of T + K - 2 columns
+    # per slot and channel, viewed as [T, dim, K - 1] windows with step stride ==
+    # window stride.
+    num_cols = seqlen + width - 2
+    if case == "window_axis_0":
+        shared = torch.randn(num_slots, num_cols, dim, device=device, dtype=itype)
+        col_stride, dim_stride = shared.stride(1), shared.stride(2)
+    else:
+        shared = torch.randn(num_slots, dim, num_cols, device=device, dtype=itype)
+        dim_stride, col_stride = shared.stride(1), shared.stride(2)
+    dedup = shared.as_strided(
+        (num_slots, seqlen, dim, width - 1),
+        (shared.stride(0), col_stride, dim_stride, col_stride),
+    )
+    dense = torch.randn(num_slots, seqlen, dim, width - 1, device=device, dtype=itype)
+    shared_before, dense_before = shared.clone(), dense.clone()
+
+    def run(window):
+        state = conv_state.clone()
+        out = causal_conv1d_update(
+            x,
+            state,
+            weight,
+            bias,
+            activation="silu",
+            conv_state_indices=conv_state_indices,
+            num_accept_tokens=num_accept_tokens,
+            intermediate_conv_window=window,
+            intermediate_state_indices=window_indices,
+            pad_slot_id=PAD_SLOT_ID,
+        )
+        return out, state
+
+    out_tile, state_tile = run(dedup)
+    out_ref, state_ref = run(dense)
+
+    # Each real row's shared window row is [state[o + 1], state[o + 2], x_0, ...,
+    # x_{T-1}] with o = num_accept_tokens - 1 (0 without num_accept_tokens).
+    offset = torch.zeros(batch, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+    if num_accept_tokens is not None:
+        offset = num_accept_tokens.long() - 1
+    prior_cols = offset[real, None] + torch.arange(1, width - 1, device=device)
+    prior = conv_state[conv_state_indices[real].long()].gather(
+        2, prior_cols[:, None, :].expand(-1, dim, -1)
+    )
+    rows = torch.cat([prior, x[real]], dim=-1)
+    written = window_indices[real].long()
+    expected_shared = shared_before.clone()
+    expected_shared[written] = rows.transpose(1, 2) if case == "window_axis_0" else rows
+    expected_dense = dense_before.clone()
+    expected_dense[written] = rows.unfold(-1, width - 1, 1).transpose(1, 2)
+
+    # Windows and conv states are copies, so they must match bitwise.
+    assert torch.equal(shared, expected_shared)
+    assert torch.equal(dense, expected_dense)
+    assert torch.equal(dedup[written], dense[written])
+    assert torch.equal(state_tile, state_ref)
+    rtol, atol = (3e-4, 1e-3) if itype == torch.float32 else (1e-2, 5e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_tile[real], out_ref[real], rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

+"""Packed (varlen) causal_conv1d_update for ragged speculative verify.
+
+A packed call must match the dense call on the same tokens, each sequence
+zero-padded to the draft width, bit for bit: the real output rows, the conv
+state and the intermediate conv windows (both the dense per-step layout and
+the deduplicated overlapping one). Sequences without a state slot or without
+rows, and packed rows past the last sequence, touch no state. Also checks
+CUDA-graph replay against eager.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=40, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+    pytest.skip("packed causal_conv1d_update needs CUDA", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import (  # noqa: E402
+    causal_conv1d_update,
+)
+
+DEV = "cuda"
+WIDTH = 4
+
+
+def _window_buffers(num_rows, dim, draft_tokens, dtype, dedup):
+    """Intermediate conv window as the mamba pool allocates it: the physical
+    buffer plus the [rows, step, dim, width - 1] view the kernel writes."""
+    win = WIDTH - 1
+    if dedup:
+        phys = torch.randn(num_rows, dim, draft_tokens + win - 1, device=DEV)
+        phys = phys.to(dtype)
+        view = phys.as_strided(
+            (num_rows, draft_tokens, dim, win),
+            (phys.stride(0), phys.stride(2), phys.stride(1), phys.stride(2)),
+        )
+        return phys, view
+    phys = torch.randn(num_rows, draft_tokens, dim, win, device=DEV).to(dtype)
+    return phys, phys
+
+
+class _Case:
+    def __init__(self, lens, slots, *, dim, draft_tokens, dtype, dedup, tail=0):
+        self.lens = list(lens)
+        self.slots = list(slots)
+        self.dim = dim
+        self.T = draft_tokens
+        self.dtype = dtype
+        self.dedup = dedup
+        bs = len(self.lens)
+        self.num_tokens = sum(self.lens) + tail
+        num_slots = max(self.slots + [0]) + 2
+        g = torch.Generator(device=DEV).manual_seed(1234 + bs + tail)
+        self.x = torch.randn(
+            self.num_tokens, dim, device=DEV, dtype=torch.float32, generator=g
+        ).to(dtype)
+        self.weight = torch.randn(
+            dim, WIDTH, device=DEV, dtype=torch.float32, generator=g
+        ).to(dtype)
+        self.bias = torch.randn(dim, device=DEV, dtype=torch.float32, generator=g)
+        self.bias = self.bias.to(dtype)
+        self.conv_state = torch.randn(
+            num_slots, dim, WIDTH - 1, device=DEV, dtype=torch.float32, generator=g
+        ).to(dtype)
+        # Scratch rows are positional (row i of the batch), plus a spare row.
+        self.win_phys, self.win_view = _window_buffers(
+            bs + 1, dim, draft_tokens, dtype, dedup
+        )
+        self.qsl = torch.zeros(bs + 1, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
+        self.qsl[1:] = torch.cumsum(torch.tensor(self.lens, device=DEV), 0)
+        self.slot_t = torch.tensor(self.slots, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
+        self.row_t = torch.arange(bs, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    def run_packed(self, conv_state, win_view, qsl=None):
+        return causal_conv1d_update(
+            self.x,
+            conv_state,
+            self.weight,
+            self.bias,
+            "silu",
+            conv_state_indices=self.slot_t,
+            intermediate_conv_window=win_view,
+            intermediate_state_indices=self.row_t,
+            query_start_loc=self.qsl if qsl is None else qsl,
+            max_seqlen=self.T,
+        )
+
+    def run_reference(self, conv_state, win_view):
+        """The dense call (token-major x, like the GDN dense verify) on the
+        same tokens, each sequence zero-padded to the draft width."""
+        dense = self.x.new_zeros(len(self.lens), self.T, self.dim)
+        start = 0
+        for i, n in enumerate(self.lens):
+            dense[i, :n] = self.x[start : start + n]
+            start += n
+        out = causal_conv1d_update(
+            dense.transpose(1, 2),
+            conv_state,
+            self.weight,
+            self.bias,
+            "silu",
+            conv_state_indices=self.slot_t,
+            intermediate_conv_window=win_view,
+            intermediate_state_indices=self.row_t,
+        )
+        return out.transpose(1, 2)
+
+
+def _check(case: _Case):
+    ref_state = case.conv_state.clone()
+    ref_win_phys = case.win_phys.clone()
+    ref_win_view = ref_win_phys.as_strided(case.win_view.shape, case.win_view.stride())
+    ref_out = case.run_reference(ref_state, ref_win_view)
+    # A sequence without rows exits before touching its slot or window, even
+    # when it has a slot; the padded dense call would run it on zeros.
+    for i, (n, slot) in enumerate(zip(case.lens, case.slots)):
+        if n == 0 and slot >= 0:
+            ref_state[slot] = case.conv_state[slot]
+            ref_win_phys[i] = case.win_phys[i]
+
+    state = case.conv_state.clone()
+    win_phys = case.win_phys.clone()
+    win_view = win_phys.as_strided(case.win_view.shape, case.win_view.stride())
+    out = case.run_packed(state, win_view)
+
+    assert out.shape == case.x.shape
+    start = 0
+    for i, (n, slot) in enumerate(zip(case.lens, case.slots)):
+        if slot >= 0:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                out[start : start + n], ref_out[i, :n], rtol=0, atol=0
+            )
+        start += n
+    # Every state byte matches: rows without a slot or without tokens and the
+    # tier leftovers wrote nothing.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(state, ref_state, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(win_phys, ref_win_phys, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+LAYOUTS = {
+    # name: (verify lens, mamba slots, tier leftovers)
+    "all_full": ([8, 8, 8, 8], [3, 0, 5, 1], 0),
+    "mixed": ([1, 8, 3, 5, 2, 7, 4, 6], [7, 2, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 4], 0),
+    "zero_length_rows": ([3, 0, 5, 0, 0, 1], [2, -1, 4, -1, -1, 0], 0),
+    "null_slots": ([4, 2, 8, 3, 3], [1, -1, 0, -1, -1], 0),
+    "zero_length_with_slot": ([3, 0, 5, 0, 2], [2, 4, 0, -1, 1], 0),
+    "tier_leftovers": ([2, 5, 8, 1], [0, 2, 1, 3], 13),
+    "single_token_rows": ([1, 1, 1], [2, 0, 1], 0),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", list(LAYOUTS))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dedup", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dim", [768, 1000])
+def test_packed_rows_match_padded_dense(layout, dedup, dtype, dim):
+    lens, slots, tail = LAYOUTS[layout]
+    _check(
+        _Case(lens, slots, dim=dim, draft_tokens=8, dtype=dtype, dedup=dedup, tail=tail)
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("draft_tokens", [2, 4, 16])
+def test_packed_rows_other_widths(draft_tokens):
+    lens = [draft_tokens, 1, max(1, draft_tokens // 2), 0, draft_tokens - 1 or 1]
+    slots = [0, 3, 1, -1, 2]
+    _check(
+        _Case(
+            lens,
+            slots,
+            dim=512,
+            draft_tokens=draft_tokens,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            dedup=True,
+            tail=3,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_replay_matches_eager():
+    """One capture serves every layout of the same row count."""
+    T, dim = 8, 640
+    capture_lens = [2] * 8
+    slots = [5, 2, 7, 0, -1, 3, -1, 1]
+    case = _Case(
+        capture_lens,
+        slots,
+        dim=dim,
+        draft_tokens=T,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        dedup=True,
+        tail=0,
+    )
+    qsl_buf = case.qsl.clone()
+    state = case.conv_state.clone()
+    phys = case.win_phys.clone()
+    view = phys.as_strided(case.win_view.shape, case.win_view.stride())
+
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        case.run_packed(state, view, qsl_buf)  # warm up / compile
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        out_graph = case.run_packed(state, view, qsl_buf)
+
+    for lens in ([1, 3, 0, 4, 0, 2, 1, 5], [8, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 2, 3], [0] * 8):
+        assert sum(lens) <= case.num_tokens
+        qsl = torch.zeros(len(lens) + 1, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
+        qsl[1:] = torch.cumsum(torch.tensor(lens, device=DEV), 0)
+
+        eager_state = case.conv_state.clone()
+        eager_phys = case.win_phys.clone()
+        eager_view = eager_phys.as_strided(case.win_view.shape, case.win_view.stride())
+        eager = case.run_packed(eager_state, eager_view, qsl)
+
+        state.copy_(case.conv_state)
+        phys.copy_(case.win_phys)
+        qsl_buf.copy_(qsl)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        n = int(qsl[-1])
+        real = torch.zeros(case.num_tokens, dtype=torch.bool, device=DEV)
+        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(qsl[:-1].tolist(), qsl[1:].tolist())):
+            if slots[i] >= 0:
+                real[s:e] = True
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_graph[real], eager[real], rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(state, eager_state, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(phys, eager_phys, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        assert n <= case.num_tokens
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

+"""DFLASH under confidence-scheduled verify on the device: sampling acceptance
+stops at the planned verify length, and the lagged confidence relay resolves
+the same copy on every rank."""
+
+import types
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.managers import overlap_utils
+from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_worker_v2 as worker_mod
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+
+
+def _selector_accept(candidates, target_tokens, cutoff_verify_lens):
+    """Selector sampling acceptance with a one-hot draft q on each drawn token
+    and a target that puts all of its mass on target_tokens, so every
+    acceptance and bonus is determined."""
+    bs, block = candidates.shape
+    vocab = 32
+    other = (candidates[:, 1:] + 1) % vocab
+    candidate_ids = torch.stack((candidates[:, 1:], other), dim=-1)
+    q_rows = torch.zeros(candidate_ids.shape, device=DEVICE)
+    q_rows[..., 0] = 1.0
+    target_logits = torch.zeros(bs * block, vocab, device=DEVICE)
+    target_logits.scatter_(1, target_tokens.reshape(-1, 1), 100.0)
+
+    worker = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        _selector_sample=(candidate_ids, q_rows),
+        _draft_probs_buf=None,
+        _block_verification=False,
+        _tp_sync=types.SimpleNamespace(sync=lambda site, tensor: tensor),
+        block_size=block,
+    )
+    worker._selector_sampling_accept = types.MethodType(
+        worker_mod.DFlashWorkerV2._selector_sampling_accept, worker
+    )
+    return worker_mod.DFlashWorkerV2._accept_block(
+        worker,
+        candidates=candidates,
+        next_token_logits=target_logits,
+        sampling_info=types.SimpleNamespace(
+            temperatures=torch.ones(bs, 1, device=DEVICE),
+            need_top_k_sampling=False,
+            need_top_p_sampling=False,
+        ),
+        draft_input=None,
+        prefix_lens=torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE),
+        bs=bs,
+        cutoff_verify_lens=cutoff_verify_lens,
+    )
+
+
+class TestDFlashRaggedVerify(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_selector_sampling_accept_stops_at_planned_verify_len(self):
+        # Rows 0 and 2 draft the target's tokens; row 1 misses its second draft.
+        candidates = torch.tensor(
+            [[9, 1, 2, 3, 4], [9, 5, 6, 7, 8], [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]], device=DEVICE
+        )
+        target_tokens = torch.tensor(
+            [[1, 2, 3, 4, 20], [5, 21, 7, 8, 22], [10, 11, 12, 13, 23]],
+            device=DEVICE,
+        )
+
+        full = _selector_accept(candidates, target_tokens, None)
+        self.assertEqual(full[0].tolist(), [4, 1, 4])
+        self.assertEqual(full[2].tolist(), [20, 21, 23])
+
+        accept_len, commit_lens, bonus, out_tokens, _, cap_trim_lens = _selector_accept(
+            candidates,
+            target_tokens,
+            torch.tensor([3, 5, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        )
+        # Each request accepts at most verify_len - 1 drafts and takes its bonus
+        # from its last verified row; the cutoff trims the rest.
+        self.assertEqual(accept_len.tolist(), [2, 1, 0])
+        self.assertEqual(bonus.tolist(), [3, 21, 10])
+        self.assertEqual(cap_trim_lens.tolist(), [2, 0, 4])
+        self.assertEqual(commit_lens.tolist(), [3, 2, 1])
+        self.assertEqual(out_tokens[0, :3].tolist(), [1, 2, 3])
+
+    def test_relay_resolves_the_lagged_copy_while_it_is_in_flight(self):
+        lag = overlap_utils.CONFIDENCE_RELAY_RING_LAG
+        relay = overlap_utils.ConfidenceRelay(
+            device=DEVICE,
+            req_pool_size=4,
+            pool=types.SimpleNamespace(
+                req_generation=torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int64)
+            ),
+        )
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        indices = torch.tensor([1, 2], device=DEVICE)
+        ready = None
+        for step in range(lag):
+            relay.scatter(indices, torch.full((2, 3), step + 1.0, device=DEVICE))
+            ready = torch.cuda.Event()
+            ready.record()
+            # Hold the ring copy in flight behind a busy side stream.
+            with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+                torch.cuda._sleep(100_000_000)
+            relay.issue_ring_copy(stream=side, publish_ready=ready)
+
+        batch = types.SimpleNamespace(
+            spec_info=types.SimpleNamespace(future_indices=torch.tensor([0])),
+            req_pool_indices_cpu=torch.tensor([1, 2]),
+        )
+        # The copy of the first step is still queued: resolving waits for it
+        # rather than returning nothing, and the next scatter did not overwrite
+        # the buffer it reads.
+        resolved = relay.resolve(batch, stream=side, publish_ready=ready)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(resolved)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(resolved.confidence, torch.full((2, 3), 1.0))
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""DFLASH on DSpark's confidence-scheduled verify: the planner takes the worker's
+confidence, acceptance stops at the planned verify length, and the confidence
+feature reads the selector row each draft token came from."""
+
+import types
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.models.dflash import CandidateSelector
+from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_worker_v2 as worker_mod
+from sglang.srt.speculative.dspark_components import dspark_planner
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _greedy_accept(candidates, target_predict, cutoff_verify_lens):
+    worker = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        _selector_sample=None,
+        _tp_sync=types.SimpleNamespace(sync=lambda site, tensor: tensor),
+        _use_triton_accept_bonus=False,
+        block_size=candidates.shape[1],
+    )
+    return worker_mod.DFlashWorkerV2._accept_block(
+        worker,
+        candidates=candidates,
+        next_token_logits=None,
+        sampling_info=None,
+        draft_input=None,
+        prefix_lens=torch.tensor([10, 20]),
+        bs=candidates.shape[0],
+        target_predict=target_predict,
+        cutoff_verify_lens=cutoff_verify_lens,
+    )
+
+
+def test_greedy_accept_stops_at_planned_verify_len():
+    # Row 0's drafts all match; row 1 mismatches at its third draft.
+    candidates = torch.tensor([[5, 1, 2, 3, 4], [6, 7, 8, 0, 9]])
+    target_predict = torch.tensor([[1, 2, 3, 4, 11], [7, 8, 12, 13, 14]])
+
+    full = _greedy_accept(candidates, target_predict, None)
+    assert full[0].tolist() == [4, 2]
+    assert full[5] is None
+
+    accept_len, commit_lens, bonus, out_tokens, _, cap_trim_lens = _greedy_accept(
+        candidates, target_predict, torch.tensor([3, 5], dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+    # Row 0 verified 2 drafts: it keeps them and takes the target token after
+    # the last verified row as its bonus. Row 1 rejected inside its window.
+    assert accept_len.tolist() == [2, 2]
+    assert cap_trim_lens.tolist() == [2, 0]
+    assert bonus.tolist() == [3, 12]
+    assert commit_lens.tolist() == [3, 3]
+    assert out_tokens[:, :3].tolist() == [[1, 2, 3], [7, 8, 12]]
+
+
+def test_greedy_accept_with_full_verify_len_matches_static():
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    candidates = torch.randint(0, 4, (16, 8))
+    target_predict = torch.randint(0, 4, (16, 8))
+    static = _greedy_accept(candidates, target_predict, None)
+    capped = _greedy_accept(
+        candidates, target_predict, torch.full((16,), 8, dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+    for got, ref in zip(capped[:4], static[:4]):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got.long(), ref.long())
+    assert capped[5].tolist() == [0] * 16
+
+
+class _RecordingEstimator:
+    def feature_and_predict(self, scores, temperatures):
+        self.scores, self.temperatures = scores, temperatures
+        return scores.amax(dim=-1), scores.amax(dim=-1).sigmoid()
+
+
+def test_feature_scores_the_selector_row_each_token_was_drawn_from():
+    selector = CandidateSelector(hidden_size=4, vocab_size=64, state_rank=2, top_k=4)
+    torch.manual_seed(3)
+    bs, slots, top_k = 3, 5, 4
+    candidate_ids = torch.stack(
+        [torch.randperm(64)[: slots * top_k].view(slots, top_k) for _ in range(bs)]
+    )
+    scores = torch.randn(bs, slots, top_k, top_k)
+    temperatures = torch.tensor([0.7, 1.3, 1e-5])
+    greedy_mask = torch.tensor([False, False, True])
+    tokens, _ = selector.sample_path(
+        candidate_ids=candidate_ids,
+        scores=scores,
+        uniforms=torch.rand(bs, slots),
+        temperatures=temperatures,
+        greedy_mask=greedy_mask,
+    )
+
+    estimator = _RecordingEstimator()
+    worker_mod._walked_confidence(
+        estimator,
+        candidate_ids=candidate_ids,
+        scores=scores,
+        tokens=tokens,
+        temperatures=temperatures,
+        greedy_mask=greedy_mask,
+    )
+
+    for b in range(bs):
+        previous = 0
+        for slot in range(slots):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                estimator.scores[b, slot], scores[b, slot, previous]
+            )
+            previous = int((candidate_ids[b, slot] == tokens[b, slot]).nonzero())
+    # A greedy row is scored at temperature 1, a sampled row at its own.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(estimator.temperatures, torch.tensor([0.7, 1.3, 1.0]))
+

+def _patch_planner_context(monkeypatch):
+    spec = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        speculative_dspark_align_verify_tokens_to_graph_tier=False,
+        speculative_dspark_confidence_sts_path=None,
+        speculative_dspark_sps_table_path=None,

+    monkeypatch.setattr(dspark_planner, "get_spec", lambda: spec)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        dspark_planner,
+        "get_schedule",
+        lambda: types.SimpleNamespace(
+            disable_overlap_schedule=False, max_running_requests=4
+        ),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dspark_planner, "is_dp_attention_enabled", lambda: False)
+
+
+def _planner(*, external_confidence):
+    return dspark_planner.DSparkVerifyPlanner(
+        draft_model=types.SimpleNamespace(),
+        gamma=3,
+        model_runner=types.SimpleNamespace(decode_cuda_graph_runner=None),
+        device=torch.device("cpu"),

+def test_planner_schedules_external_confidence_without_a_head(monkeypatch):
+    _patch_planner_context(monkeypatch)
+    with envs.SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE.override("cap-accept"):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="confidence head"):
+            _planner(external_confidence=False)
+        planner = _planner(external_confidence=True)
+        assert planner.schedules_verify_budget and planner.carries_confidence
+
+        confidence = torch.tensor(
+            [[0.9, 0.9, 0.9], [0.2, 0.9, 0.9], [0.9, 0.8, 0.1]], dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        layout = planner.schedule_layout(
+            req_pool_indices=torch.tensor([1, 2, 3]),
+            prefix_lens=torch.tensor([5, 6, 7]),
+            device=torch.device("cpu"),
+            confidence=confidence,
+            budget=4,
+        )
+    # The four most likely drafts by survival: request 0's three and request
+    # 2's first; each request also verifies its anchor.
+    assert layout.verify_lens.tolist() == [4, 1, 2]

+def test_compact_plan_on_the_full_block_graph_verifies_every_draft(monkeypatch):
+    _patch_planner_context(monkeypatch)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        dspark_planner,
+        "build_sps_cost_table",
+        lambda **_: dspark_planner.SpsCostTable(
+            sample_batch_tokens=[1, 16],
+            sample_steps_per_sec=[2.0, 1.0],
+            max_batch_tokens=16,
+        ),
+    )
+    # Compact graphs of 4, 8, 12 and 16 tokens for blocks of 4 tokens.
+    runner = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        ragged_verify_mode=True, capture_num_tokens=[4, 8, 12, 16], max_bs=4
+    )
+    with envs.SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE.override("compact"):
+        planner = dspark_planner.DSparkVerifyPlanner(
+            draft_model=types.SimpleNamespace(),
+            gamma=3,
+            model_runner=types.SimpleNamespace(decode_cuda_graph_runner=runner),
+            device=torch.device("cpu"),
+            tp_rank=1,
+            verify_num_draft_tokens=4,
+            tp_sync=types.SimpleNamespace(sync=lambda site, tensor: tensor),
+            external_confidence=True,
+        )
+
+        def plan(bs, budget):
+            return planner.schedule_layout(
+                req_pool_indices=torch.arange(1, bs + 1),
+                prefix_lens=torch.full((bs,), 5),
+                device=torch.device("cpu"),
+                confidence=torch.tensor([[0.9, 0.5, 0.1]] * bs),
+                budget=budget,
+            )
+
+        # Any plan of a single request replays the 4-token graph of its block.
+        assert not planner.plans_verify_budget(num_reqs=1)
+        single = plan(1, 0)
+        assert single.is_full_block(4) and plan(1, 2) is single
+
+        # Three requests: 9 planned tokens replay the 12-token graph of the
+        # full blocks, so every draft is verified; 7 fit the 8-token graph.
+        assert planner.plans_verify_budget(num_reqs=3)
+        full = plan(3, 6)
+        assert full.is_full_block(4) and full.verify_lens.tolist() == [4, 4, 4]
+        trimmed = plan(3, 4)
+        assert not trimmed.is_full_block(4)
+        assert trimmed.graph_num_tokens == 8 and int(trimmed.verify_lens.sum()) == 7
+

+"""GDN ReplaySSM spec-verify ring: configuration checks and commit routing.
+
+Under ``--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`` a GDN verify appends the draft window
+to a compact request ring of ``--linear-replayssm-cache-len`` positions and the
+commit folds the accepted prefix into the checkpoint. DSPARK and DFLASH commit
+through ``HybridLinearAttnBackend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify``, which
+goes through the same ring commit as the generic spec commit.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.arg_groups.attention_hook import handle_linear_attn_backend
+from sglang.srt.configs.mamba_utils import (
+    Mamba2CacheParams,
+    Mamba2StateDType,
+    Mamba2StateShape,
+)
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.hybrid_linear_attn_backend import (
+    HybridLinearAttnBackend,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.gdn_backend import (
+    _validate_gdn_target_verify_layout,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import MambaPool
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import override_platform
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=15, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_KERNELS = "sglang.kernels.ops.attention.linear.gdn_replayssm_spec_decode"
+_BACKEND = "sglang.srt.layers.attention.hybrid_linear_attn_backend"
+_GDN_COMMIT = f"{_KERNELS}.commit_gdn_replayssm_after_verify"
+DRAFT_TOKENS = 8
+
+
+def _gdn_cache_params(num_layers=2):
+    shape = Mamba2StateShape.create(
+        tp_world_size=1,
+        intermediate_size=64,
+        n_groups=2,
+        num_heads=4,
+        head_dim=16,
+        state_size=16,
+        conv_kernel=4,
+    )
+    dtype = Mamba2StateDType(conv=torch.bfloat16, temporal=torch.bfloat16)
+    return Mamba2CacheParams(shape=shape, dtype=dtype, layers=list(range(num_layers)))
+
+
+def _spec_state(*, intermediate_ssm=None, temporal_dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    temporal = torch.zeros(1, 8, 2, 4, 4, dtype=temporal_dtype)
+    return MambaPool.SpeculativeState(
+        conv=[torch.zeros(1, 8, 3, 2)],
+        temporal=temporal,
+        intermediate_ssm=intermediate_ssm,
+        intermediate_conv_window=[torch.zeros(1, 4, DRAFT_TOKENS, 3, 2)],
+        replayssm_d=torch.zeros(1, 4, 2, 16, 4),
+    )
+
+
+def _gdn_pool():
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        replayssm_is_kda=False,
+        replayssm_spec_fold=False,
+        replayssm_spec_write_pos=torch.zeros(40, dtype=torch.int32),
+        replayssm_cache_base=torch.zeros(40, dtype=torch.int32),
+        replayssm_is_flush=torch.zeros(40, dtype=torch.int8),
+    )
+
+
+def _hybrid_backend(mamba_pool, spec_state, cache_indices):
+    """A HybridLinearAttnBackend whose sidecar translates virtual mamba ids by
+    +100, so the test can tell translated ids from raw ones."""
+    req_to_token_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        mamba_pool=mamba_pool,
+        get_speculative_mamba2_params_all_layers=lambda: spec_state,
+        get_mamba_indices=lambda rows: rows // 2,
+        short_conv_pool=SimpleNamespace(conv_state=None, intermediate_conv_state=None),
+        ngram_pool=SimpleNamespace(context=None, intermediate_context=None),
+    )
+    hybrid = HybridLinearAttnBackend.__new__(HybridLinearAttnBackend)
+    hybrid.linear_attn_backend = SimpleNamespace(
+        req_to_token_pool=req_to_token_pool,

+class TestGDNReplaySSMBackendCommit(CustomTestCase):
+    def _commit(self, hybrid, last_correct, req_rows, **kwargs):
+        hybrid.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify(
+            last_correct_step_indices=last_correct,
+            mamba_track_indices=kwargs.get("track_indices"),
+            mamba_steps_to_track=kwargs.get("track_steps"),
+            model=None,
+            req_pool_indices=req_rows,
+        )
+
+    def test_gdn_ring_commit_replaces_snapshot_scatter(self):
+        pool, state = _gdn_pool(), _spec_state()
+        # Rows past the request count are graph padding (state -1).
+        hybrid = _hybrid_backend(pool, state, torch.tensor([5, 9, 2, -1]))
+        req_rows = torch.tensor([17, 23, 31, 0])
+        with (
+            patch(_GDN_COMMIT) as commit,
+            patch(f"{_BACKEND}.scatter_mamba_states_after_mtp_verify") as scatter,
+        ):
+            self._commit(hybrid, torch.tensor([2, 0, 7]), req_rows)
+
+        scatter.assert_not_called()
+        commit.assert_called_once()
+        kwargs = commit.call_args.kwargs
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["spec_state"], state)
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["state_batch_indices"].tolist(), [5, 9, 2])
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["replay_indices"].tolist(), [17, 23, 31])
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["accept_lens"].tolist(), [3, 1, 8])
+        # Every accepted window folds, so `temporal` is the committed state.
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["fold_every_commit"], True)
+
+    def test_pp_rows_and_track_slots_are_translated(self):
+        pool, state = _gdn_pool(), _spec_state()
+        hybrid = _hybrid_backend(pool, state, torch.tensor([7, 7, 7]))
+        req_rows = torch.tensor([14, 22, 30])
+        track_steps = torch.tensor([1, -1, 5])
+        with (
+            patch(_GDN_COMMIT) as commit,
+            patch(f"{_BACKEND}.pp_spec_stable_rows_enabled", return_value=True),
+        ):
+            self._commit(
+                hybrid,
+                torch.tensor([3, 0, 6]),
+                req_rows,
+                track_indices=torch.tensor([40, 41, 42]),
+                track_steps=track_steps,
+            )
+
+        kwargs = commit.call_args.kwargs
+        # PP stable rows read the slots of the delayed batch's request rows.
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["state_batch_indices"].tolist(), [107, 111, 115])
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["src_indices_raw"].tolist(), [14, 22, 30])
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["replay_indices"].tolist(), [14, 22, 30])
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["mamba_track_indices"].tolist(), [140, 141, 142])
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["mamba_steps_to_track"], track_steps)
+        self.assertEqual(kwargs["accept_lens"].tolist(), [4, 1, 7])
+
+    def test_empty_batch_is_noop(self):
+        hybrid = _hybrid_backend(_gdn_pool(), _spec_state(), torch.tensor([-1]))

+    def test_snapshot_scatter_requires_snapshots(self):

+        cache_indices = torch.tensor([5, 9])
+        last_correct = torch.tensor([1, 0])
+        req_rows = torch.tensor([3, 4])
+
+        hybrid = _hybrid_backend(pool, _spec_state(), cache_indices)
+        with (
+            patch(f"{_BACKEND}.scatter_mamba_states_after_mtp_verify") as scatter,
